Today’s M&A briefing — 16 deals, the strategies behind them · 12 November 2026

🔹 Oura (smart rings continuously measuring heart rate) acquires Counsel Health.

🔹 Allemagne (sovereign state) acquires a stake in KNDS (franco-German group manufacturing tanks and land weapon systems, including the Leopard 2 tank).
KNDS was formed from the merger of Krauss-Maffei Wegmann and Nexter. Berlin wanted equal weight with Paris in the group's strategic decisions, particularly on export choices and program development.

🔹 Raenest (financial platform for sending, receiving) acquires Remitise (UK payment company registered with the Financial Conduct Authority).
Raenest already holds licenses in Canada and Nigeria. The acquisition of Remitise gives it a direct regulatory foothold in the UK, a central market for international payment flows.

🔹 Gustoso acquires Familie Wiesner Gastronomie.

🔹 Ondas (US group developing military surveillance drones via its Ondas Sentinel division) acquires Stemme (german manufacturer of certified motor gliders).

🔹 Kohl Medical (homecare provider in Germany) acquires Livica (national homecare provider in Germany).

🔹 Altia Energy (colombian energy group with a historical activity of gas thermal generation via Termoyopal) acquires Isagen's 219 MW renewable portfolio (five photovoltaic plants).

🔹 club deal coordinated by Findi Investimenti and ANMO acquires Groupe Poppi (Poppi Ugo Euroforge S.p.A., Elettrostamperie Italia S.p.A., Italgear S.r.l.).

🔹 Serescentia acquires ENS (nutraceutical company with proprietary brands).

🔹 Marventa Group (dutch group of maritime equipment and services) acquires Holland Nautic (dutch specialist in marine electronics and navigation systems).

🔹 Rapleys (UK property consultancy, present) acquires Northmill Associates (14-person architectural firm founded in 2016).

🔹 Agiliti Group (waste management group based in Cannock) acquires Forward Waste Management (welsh company managing complex industrial and manufacturing waste).

🔹 Zinzino acquires Uzesta.
The operation strengthens Zinzino's presence in the North American market.

🔹 Kreeft Opleidingen (training center based in Hoogeveen, Drenthe) finalizes the acquisition of Rijschool Bruinsma's heavy transport training activities (C license) (c license training, heavy transport from a Utrecht driving school declared bankrupt, including four trucks).

🔹 Vissers Ploegmakers (dutch family business) acquires BouwOort (ready-mix concrete producer in the Netherlands).

🔹 H.M. Verploegen (family transporter from Wijchen) finalizes the acquisition of Croonen Transport (family transporter from Nijmegen).

🔹 Vissers Ploegmakers (entreprise familiale néerlandaise, liée à InfraHUB B.V. et BovOss B.V) rachète BouwOort (producteur de béton prêt à l'emploi aux Pays-Bas).

en.text:
Today’s fundraising briefing — 6 deals, the strategies behind them · 12 November 2026

🔹 Vaeridion (nine-passenger electric aircraft with glider-inspired wing, multi-engine propulsion, and patented modular batteries) — more than €124m · Series A2.
Vaeridion claims provisional purchase commitments for over 130 aircraft for more than €730M, with ASL Group as launch customer. KLM, BayernLB, and TrueNoord sit on its advisory board. Preliminary design review is complete.
𝗨𝘀𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗱𝘀: Finance a final assembly line at Oberpfaffenhofen airport via the EU Innovation Fund grant (CAROLUS project).
𝗜𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀: SHIFT Invest and Invest-NL (co-leads), World Fund, Project A, Vsquared Ventures, Alexander Rittweger (founder) — for the €30M equity tranche.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: 76% of the announced envelope is public money and the 130 orders are provisional agreements: this round finances demonstration, not yet commercial commissioning.

🔹 Sparxity (sparse-native AI chips and computing architectures, activating only useful parts of a model with each computation) — $90m · Series A.
Three manufacturing cycles completed, over 70,000 chips produced, 12 racks deployed at over 30 clients including supercomputing centers. Revenue quadrupled between 2024 and 2025.
𝗨𝘀𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗱𝘀: Accelerate the development of specialized chips aiming for up to 44 times faster inference on ultra-sparse models.
𝗜𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀: ICM HPQC Fund (lead), Lockheed Martin Ventures, GlobalFoundries, GS Futures, Cloudberry Ventures, TGFS, EIC Fund, and business angels including Richard Socher and Nancy Xu.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: The presence of Lockheed Martin Ventures and GlobalFoundries signals that dynamic sparsity is of interest to defense applications as much as commercial cloud, and that the manufacturing chain is already under discussion.

🔹 Tendrils (new general-purpose processor architecture running thousands of cores in parallel via interaction nets, founded in 2025) — €26m · Seed.
Founded by Nils Cremer, who studied interaction nets at ETH Zürich. Co-founders developed Vine (open-source language) and contributed to OpenTitan at lowRISC.
𝗜𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀: Benchmark (lead, Jack Altman on board), Visionaries Club, UK Sovereign AI Fund, FR8, Antimatter, Cloudberry VC, Conviction, Embassy Ventures, SV Angels.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: The combination of the UK Sovereign AI Fund and Benchmark signals that sovereignty over computing architectures is now an industrial policy issue, not just a market one.

🔹 TiLT Capital Partners — €12.4m.

🔹 Switchpoint Bio — €4.75m · pre-Seed.

🔹 ION Video (video virtualization technology aiming to reduce video file size and lighten data center load) — $692,000.

🔹 Vaeridion (𝑎𝑣𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑒́𝑙𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑛𝑒𝑢𝑓 𝑝𝑎𝑠𝑠𝑎𝑔𝑒𝑟𝑠 𝑎̀ 𝑎𝑖𝑙𝑒 𝑖𝑛𝑠𝑝𝑖𝑟𝑒́𝑒 𝑑𝑢 𝑝𝑙𝑎𝑛𝑒𝑢𝑟, 𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑝𝑢𝑙𝑠𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑚𝑢𝑙𝑡𝑖-𝑚𝑜𝑡𝑒𝑢𝑟𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑏𝑎𝑡𝑡𝑒𝑟𝑖𝑒𝑠 𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑢𝑙𝑎𝑖𝑟𝑒𝑠 𝑏𝑟𝑒𝑣𝑒𝑡𝑒́𝑒𝑠) — plus de 124 M€ · Série A2.
Vaeridion revendique des engagements d'achat provisoires sur plus de 130 appareils pour plus de 730 M€, avec ASL Group comme client de lancement. KLM, BayernLB et TrueNoord siègent à son comité consultatif. La revue de conception préliminaire est achevée.
𝗢𝗯𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗳 : Financer une ligne d'assemblage final à l'aéroport d'Oberpfaffenhofen via la subvention EU Innovation Fund (projet CAROLUS).
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : 76 % de l'enveloppe annoncée est de l'argent public et les 130 commandes sont des accords provisoires : ce tour finance la démonstration, pas encore la mise en service commerciale.

🔹 Sparxity (𝑝𝑢𝑐𝑒𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑎𝑟𝑐ℎ𝑖𝑡𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑢𝑟𝑒𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑐𝑎𝑙𝑐𝑢𝑙 𝑠𝑝𝑎𝑟𝑠𝑒-𝑛𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑣𝑒 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑙'𝐼𝐴, 𝑛'𝑎𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑣𝑎𝑛𝑡 𝑞𝑢𝑒 𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝑝𝑎𝑟𝑡𝑖𝑒𝑠 𝑢𝑡𝑖𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝑑'𝑢𝑛 𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑒̀𝑙𝑒 𝑎̀ 𝑐ℎ𝑎𝑞𝑢𝑒 𝑐𝑎𝑙𝑐𝑢𝑙) — 90 M$ · Série A.
Trois cycles de fabrication réalisés, plus de 70 000 puces produites, 12 racks déployés chez plus de 30 clients dont des centres de supercalcul. Chiffre d'affaires quadruplé entre 2024 et 2025.
𝗢𝗯𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗳 : Accélérer le développement de puces spécialisées visant une inférence jusqu'à 44 fois plus rapide sur les modèles ultra-parcimonieux.
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : La présence de Lockheed Martin Ventures et de GlobalFoundries signale que la parcimonie dynamique intéresse autant les applications de défense que le cloud commercial, et que la chaîne de fabrication est déjà en discussion.

🔹 Tendrils (𝑛𝑜𝑢𝑣𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑒 𝑎𝑟𝑐ℎ𝑖𝑡𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑢𝑟𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑐𝑒𝑠𝑠𝑒𝑢𝑟 𝑔𝑒́𝑛𝑒́𝑟𝑎𝑙𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑒 𝑓𝑎𝑖𝑠𝑎𝑛𝑡 𝑓𝑜𝑛𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑛𝑒𝑟 𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝑚𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑖𝑒𝑟𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑐œ𝑢𝑟𝑠 𝑒𝑛 𝑝𝑎𝑟𝑎𝑙𝑙𝑒̀𝑙𝑒 𝑣𝑖𝑎 𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝑖𝑛𝑡𝑒𝑟𝑎𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑛𝑒𝑡𝑠) — 26 M€ · Seed.
Fondée par Nils Cremer, qui a étudié les interaction nets à l'ETH Zürich. Co-fondateurs ayant développé Vine (langage open source) et contribué à OpenTitan chez lowRISC.

🔹 TiLT Capital Partners — 12,4 M€.
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : L'investisseur dit autant que le montant : TiLT Capital est un fonds de transition énergétique, pas un fonds SaaS généraliste.

🔹 Switchpoint Bio — 4,75 M€ · pré-Seed.

🔹 ION Video (𝑡𝑒𝑐ℎ𝑛𝑜𝑙𝑜𝑔𝑖𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑣𝑖𝑟𝑡𝑢𝑎𝑙𝑖𝑠𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑣𝑖𝑑𝑒́𝑜 𝑣𝑖𝑠𝑎𝑛𝑡 𝑎̀ 𝑟𝑒́𝑑𝑢𝑖𝑟𝑒 𝑙𝑎 𝑡𝑎𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑒 𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝑓𝑖𝑐ℎ𝑖𝑒𝑟𝑠 𝑣𝑖𝑑𝑒́𝑜 𝑒𝑡 𝑎𝑙𝑙𝑒́𝑔𝑒𝑟 𝑙𝑎 𝑐ℎ𝑎𝑟𝑔𝑒 𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝑑𝑎𝑡𝑎 𝑐𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑒𝑟𝑠) — 692 000 $.
